requirements.subject: ent:disconnect-operation
requirements.canonical: The `disconnect` operation IS the opposite operation of the `connect` operation.
requirements.original: The disconnect and unmap operations are the opposite operations of connect and map.

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-operation
requirements.canonical: The `unmap` operation IS the opposite operation of the `map` operation.
requirements.original: The disconnect and unmap operations are the opposite operations of connect and map.

requirements.subject: ent:disconnect-operation
requirements.canonical: The `disconnect` operation has the syntax disconnect optionally followed by one of ( ComponentRef : Port , ComponentRef : Port ), ( PortRef ), ( ComponentRef : all port ) or ( all component : all port ).
requirements.original:
disconnect [ ( "(" ComponentRef ":" Port "," ComponentRef ":" Port ")" ) | 
        ( "(" PortRef ")" ) |
        ( "(" ComponentRef ":" all port ")" ) |
        ( "(" all component ":" all port ")" ) ]
  unmap [ ( "(" ComponentRef ":" Port "," ComponentRef ":" Port ")" 
               [ param "(" [ { ActualPar [","] }+ ] ")" ] ) | 
      ( "(" PortRef ")" [ param "(" [ { ActualPar [","] }+ ] ")" ] ) |
      ( "(" ComponentRef ":" all port ")" ) |
      ( "(" all component ":" all port ")" ) ]

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-operation
requirements.canonical: The `unmap` operation has the syntax unmap optionally followed by one of ( ComponentRef : Port , ComponentRef : Port ) [param clause], ( PortRef ) [param clause], ( ComponentRef : all port ) or ( all component : all port ).
requirements.original:
disconnect [ ( "(" ComponentRef ":" Port "," ComponentRef ":" Port ")" ) | 
        ( "(" PortRef ")" ) |
        ( "(" ComponentRef ":" all port ")" ) |
        ( "(" all component ":" all port ")" ) ]
  unmap [ ( "(" ComponentRef ":" Port "," ComponentRef ":" Port ")" 
               [ param "(" [ { ActualPar [","] }+ ] ")" ] ) | 
      ( "(" PortRef ")" [ param "(" [ { ActualPar [","] }+ ] ")" ] ) |
      ( "(" ComponentRef ":" all port ")" ) |
      ( "(" all component ":" all port ")" ) ]

requirements.subject: ent:disconnect-operation
requirements.canonical: The `disconnect` operation disconnects previously connected ports of test components.
requirements.original: The disconnect and unmap operations perform the disconnection (of previously connected) ports of test components and the unmapping of (previously mapped) ports of test components and ports in the test system interface.

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-operation
requirements.canonical: The `unmap` operation unmaps previously mapped ports of test components and ports of the test system interface.
requirements.original: The disconnect and unmap operations perform the disconnection (of previously connected) ports of test components and the unmapping of (previously mapped) ports of test components and ports in the test system interface.

requirements.subject: ent:disconnect-operation
requirements.condition: the component references and port names are known
requirements.canonical: A `disconnect` operation MAY be called from any test component if the relevant component references and the names of the relevant ports are known.
requirements.original: Both, the disconnect and unmap operations can be called from any component if the relevant component references together with the names of the relevant ports are known.

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-operation
requirements.condition: the component references and port names are known
requirements.canonical: An `unmap` operation MAY be called from any test component if the relevant component references and the names of the relevant ports are known.
requirements.original: Both, the disconnect and unmap operations can be called from any component if the relevant component references together with the names of the relevant ports are known.

requirements.subject: ent:disconnect-operation
requirements.canonical: A `disconnect` or `unmap` operation has an effect only if the connection or mapping to be removed has been created beforehand; otherwise it has no effect.
requirements.original: A disconnect or unmap operation has only an effect if the connection or mapping to be removed has been created beforehand.

readings: A `disconnect` or `unmap` operation for a non-existing connection or mapping has no effect and test execution continues.
A `disconnect` or `unmap` operation for a non-existing connection or mapping is an error.
ambiguity.issue: The sentence does not say explicitly whether removing a non-existing connection is silently ignored or an error; the first reading (no-op, analogous to 21.1.1 for connect/map) was chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:disconnect-operation
requirements.canonical: A `disconnect` or `unmap` operation MAY be used with one argument only, to address all connections or mappings of a component or a port.
requirements.original: To ease disconnect and unmap operations related to all connections and mappings of a component or a port, it is allowed to use disconnect and unmap operations with one argument only.

requirements.subject: ent:disconnect-operation
requirements.canonical: The single argument of a `disconnect` or `unmap` operation specifies one side of the connections or mappings to be removed, and all connections or mappings of that side are removed.
requirements.original: This one argument specifies one side of the connections to be disconnected or unmapped.

requirements.subject: ent:all-port-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all port` keyword MAY be used in a `disconnect` or `unmap` operation to denote all ports of a component.
requirements.original: The all port keyword can be used to denote all ports of a component.

requirements.subject: ent:disconnect-operation
requirements.canonical: A `disconnect` or `unmap` operation without any parameters IS a shorthand form for the same operation with the parameter self:all port.
requirements.original: The usage of a disconnect or unmap operation without any parameters is a shorthand form for using the operation with the parameter self:all port.

requirements.subject: ent:disconnect-operation
requirements.canonical: A `disconnect` or `unmap` operation without parameters disconnects or unmaps all ports of the test component that calls the operation.
requirements.original: It disconnects or unmaps all ports of the component that calls the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:all-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all component` keyword SHALL only be used in combination with the `all port` keyword, i.e. as all component:all port.
requirements.original: The all component keyword shall only be used in combination with the all port keyword, i.e. all component:all port, and shall only be used by the MTC.

requirements.subject: ent:all-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all component` keyword SHALL only be used by the MTC.
requirements.original: The all component keyword shall only be used in combination with the all port keyword, i.e. all component:all port, and shall only be used by the MTC.

requirements.subject: ent:all-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: The all component:all port argument SHALL be the one and only argument of a `disconnect` or `unmap` operation.
requirements.original: Furthermore, the all component:all port argument shall be used as the one and only argument of a disconnect or unmap operation and it allows to release all connections and mappings of the test configuration.

requirements.subject: ent:all-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: A `disconnect` or `unmap` operation with the argument all component:all port releases all connections or mappings of the test configuration.
requirements.original: Furthermore, the all component:all port argument shall be used as the one and only argument of a disconnect or unmap operation and it allows to release all connections and mappings of the test configuration.

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-operation
requirements.canonical: An `unmap` operation MAY contain an optional parameter list (param clause) for configuration purposes.
requirements.original: Similar to the map operation, unmap provides an optional parameter list for configuration purposes.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the unmap operation has a parameter list
requirements.canonical: If a param clause is present in an `unmap` operation, its actual parameters SHALL conform to the unmap param clause of the port type declaration of the system port used.
requirements.original: If a parameter list is present, the actual parameters shall conform to the unmap **param clause of the port type declaration of the system** port used.

requirements.subject: ent:param-clause
requirements.canonical: The param clause of an `unmap` operation allows passing values needed for dynamic runtime configuration.
requirements.original: It allows to pass values needed for dynamic runtime configuration.

requirements.subject: ent:param-clause
requirements.canonical: In an `unmap` operation, a param clause SHALL only be present if the system port to which the param clause belongs is explicitly referenced.
requirements.original: a) In an unmap operation, a param clause shall only be present if the system port to which the param clause belongs to is explicitly referenced.

readings: A param clause is only allowed in the forms ( ComponentRef : Port , ComponentRef : Port ) and ( PortRef ) where PortRef denotes a system port by name, not with all port forms.
A param clause is only allowed in the two-operand form where the system port is explicitly named, not in the one-argument ( PortRef ) form.
ambiguity.issue: The syntax allows a param clause after ( PortRef ), but it is unclear whether a single component port reference counts as 'explicitly referencing' the mapped system port; the first reading was chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-operation
requirements.canonical: An `unmap` operation MAY omit the param clause.
requirements.original: b) In unmap operations, param clauses are optional.

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-operation
requirements.canonical: If an `unmap` operation has a param clause, exactly one of the components referenced by the operation SHALL be the system component reference.
requirements.original: If in an unmap operation a param clause is present, exactly one of the components referenced by the operation shall be the system component reference, the type of the system component shall be known in the context of the operation either via a system clause or via a runs on clause in a testcase without system clause, the type of the system port to which the operation is applied shall include an unmap param declaration and the actual parameters shall conform to the unmap **param clause of the port type declaration of the system port used.** c) If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known (either when the component reference is a variable or value returned from a function or the type is defined the runs on, mtc or system clause of the calling function), the referenced port declaration shall be present in this component type.

requirements.subject: ent:system-component
requirements.canonical: If an `unmap` operation has a param clause, the type of the system component SHALL be known in the context of the operation, either via a system clause or via the runs on clause of a testcase without system clause.
requirements.original: If in an unmap operation a param clause is present, exactly one of the components referenced by the operation shall be the system component reference, the type of the system component shall be known in the context of the operation either via a system clause or via a runs on clause in a testcase without system clause, the type of the system port to which the operation is applied shall include an unmap param declaration and the actual parameters shall conform to the unmap **param clause of the port type declaration of the system port used.** c) If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known (either when the component reference is a variable or value returned from a function or the type is defined the runs on, mtc or system clause of the calling function), the referenced port declaration shall be present in this component type.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: If an `unmap` operation has a param clause, the type of the system port to which the operation is applied SHALL include an unmap param declaration.
requirements.original: If in an unmap operation a param clause is present, exactly one of the components referenced by the operation shall be the system component reference, the type of the system component shall be known in the context of the operation either via a system clause or via a runs on clause in a testcase without system clause, the type of the system port to which the operation is applied shall include an unmap param declaration and the actual parameters shall conform to the unmap **param clause of the port type declaration of the system port used.** c) If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known (either when the component reference is a variable or value returned from a function or the type is defined the runs on, mtc or system clause of the calling function), the referenced port declaration shall be present in this component type.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: If an `unmap` operation has a param clause, its actual parameters SHALL conform to the unmap param clause of the port type declaration of the system port used.
requirements.original: If in an unmap operation a param clause is present, exactly one of the components referenced by the operation shall be the system component reference, the type of the system component shall be known in the context of the operation either via a system clause or via a runs on clause in a testcase without system clause, the type of the system port to which the operation is applied shall include an unmap param declaration and the actual parameters shall conform to the unmap **param clause of the port type declaration of the system port used.** c) If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known (either when the component reference is a variable or value returned from a function or the type is defined the runs on, mtc or system clause of the calling function), the referenced port declaration shall be present in this component type.

requirements.subject: ent:port-declaration
requirements.condition: the component type of the referenced component is known
requirements.canonical: If the type of a component referenced in a `disconnect` or `unmap` operation is known (the component reference is a variable or a value returned from a function, or the type is defined in the runs on, mtc or system clause of the calling function), the referenced port SHALL be declared in that component type.
requirements.original: If in an unmap operation a param clause is present, exactly one of the components referenced by the operation shall be the system component reference, the type of the system component shall be known in the context of the operation either via a system clause or via a runs on clause in a testcase without system clause, the type of the system port to which the operation is applied shall include an unmap param declaration and the actual parameters shall conform to the unmap **param clause of the port type declaration of the system port used.** c) If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known (either when the component reference is a variable or value returned from a function or the type is defined the runs on, mtc or system clause of the calling function), the referenced port declaration shall be present in this component type.

ambiguity.issue: 'connection operation' is not a defined term; in clause 21.1.2 it refers to disconnect and unmap.

requirements.subject: ent:disconnect-operation
requirements.canonical: The parameters of a `disconnect` operation SHALL NOT contain a system port reference.
requirements.original: d) The disconnect operation parameters shall not contain a system port reference.

requirements.subject: ent:test-case-operation
requirements.canonical: A test case operation addresses the entire test case by using the keyword `testcase`.
requirements.original: Test case operations address the entire test case by using the keyword testcase.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation IS the only test case operation.
requirements.original: Currently, the test case stop operation is the only test case operation.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation specifies an immediate stop of the test case behaviour with the verdict `error`.
requirements.original: It specifies an immediate stop of the test case behaviour with an error verdict.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation causes a user-defined immediate termination of a test case with the test verdict `error`.
requirements.original: The testcase stop operation defines a user defined immediate termination of a test case with the test verdict error and an (optional) associated reason for the termination.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation MAY specify an optional reason for the termination.
requirements.original: The testcase stop operation defines a user defined immediate termination of a test case with the test verdict error and an (optional) associated reason for the termination.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation IS intended for cases where user-defined behaviour that does not contribute to the test outcome behaves unexpectedly so that continuing the test case makes no sense.
requirements.original: Such an immediate stop of a test case is required for cases where a user defined behaviour that does not contribute to the test outcome behaves in an unexpected manner which leads to a situation where the continuation of the test case makes no more sense.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation has the syntax testcase . stop optionally followed by a parenthesized comma-separated list of FreeText or TemplateInstance items.
requirements.original: testcase "." stop [ "(" { ( FreeText | TemplateInstance ) [","] } ")" ]

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation causes an immediate stop of the entire test case behaviour with the verdict `error`.
requirements.original: The test case stop operation causes an immediate stop of the entire test case behaviour with the verdict error.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The test case stop operation writes the items in its argument, specifying the reason for the termination, to a logging device associated with the test control or the test component in which the operation is used.
requirements.original: In addition, the test case stop operation provides the means to specify the reason for the immediate termination of a test case by writing one or more items to some logging device associated with the test control or the test component in which the operation is used.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The items to be logged by a test case stop operation SHALL be given as a comma-separated list in the argument of the operation.
requirements.original: Items to be logged shall be identified by a comma-separated list in the argument of the test case stop operation.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-stop-operation
requirements.canonical: The argument of the test case stop operation SHALL follow the same restrictions as the argument of the `log` statement.
requirements.original: The argument of the test case stop operation shall follow the same restrictions as the argument of the log statement (see clause 19.11).

requirements.subject: ent:test-component-operation
requirements.canonical: Test component operations are used to create, start, stop and kill test components.
requirements.original: Test component operations are used to create, start, stop and kill test components.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component-operation
requirements.canonical: Test component operations are also used to check whether test components are alive, running, done or killed.
requirements.original: They can also be used to check if test components are alive, running, done or killed.

non_requirement.reason: introductory sentence of the restrictions list; refers to clauses 5, 21 and table 16
states that no specific restrictions beyond clause 5 and table 16 apply
